transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well… I guess I came in because I just feel real restless most of the time. Like there’s a motor running inside me all day, you know? I try not to make a big deal of it, but if I have to sit still somewhere—like church, or here at the clinic, or even at home—I start feeling kind of trapped, and I feel like I need to get up or do something. I don’t know if that makes sense.
Do you have any thoughts that keep repeating in your mind?

Um… repeating thoughts? I don’t think so, not like something stuck in my head over and over. I mean, my mind can feel busy sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’ve noticed a certain thought that keeps coming back. Is that what you mean?
Do you often feel anxious or worried?

I mean… not really, I don’t think. I worry about normal stuff, I guess, but I wouldn’t say I’m anxious all the time or anything like that. At least, I haven’t really noticed it that way. Is that what you’re asking?
Do you ever feel like you have to do certain things over and over?

Um… I don’t think so. Not like I have to keep checking something or doing some kind of routine over and over. I mean, I might do normal stuff more than once sometimes, but I haven’t noticed anything like that being a problem. Does that answer it okay?
Do you often act on impulse without thinking things through?

Yeah… I guess I do that some. I don’t mean to be rude or anything, but sometimes I jump in with an answer before the pastor, or my cousin, or even the lady at the pantry is finished talking. Then I realize I answered the wrong thing, or I made them upset. I try not to, I really do. Is that the kind of impulse you mean?
Do you feel bored or frustrated when you're feeling restless and need to get up or do something?

Yeah… I do. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but that’s kind of why I came in. It feels like I’ve got a motor running inside me all day. If I have to sit still at church, or here at the clinic, or even just at home, I start feeling trapped, like I need to get up or do something. I try to be respectful and sit there, but it gets really frustrating. Is that what you mean?
Do you often find it hard to focus on what you're doing?

Yeah… I mean, I try to pay attention. Like if folks are explaining ride times, or what I’m supposed to get from the pantry, or plans at church, I’ll be listening good at first. But then my mind just kind of slips off somewhere, and I miss pieces I needed to hear. Then I feel bad asking again, like I should’ve caught it the first time. Is that what you’re asking about?
Do you often fidget or have trouble staying seated when you're in a situation where you're supposed to be still?

Yeah… I do, though I try not to make it obvious. Like even when I’m trying to be respectful and sit still, my leg will be bouncing, or I’ll be tapping my fingers on the chair. Sometimes I’ll twist something in my hands the whole time just to keep from getting up. I hope that makes sense.
Do you often feel the need to run, climb, or engage in other physically active behaviors?

Yeah… I don’t really go running or climbing around, not like that exactly. But I do feel like I’ve got this motor in me all day, like I can’t fully settle. If I’m supposed to sit still at church, or here at the clinic, or even just at home, I start feeling trapped and like I need to get up and do something. I try to keep it under control, but it’s pretty hard. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you often talk more than others in social situations?

Um… I don’t know if I’d say I talk more than others. I mean, maybe sometimes if I’m comfortable with people, I can get going a little bit, but I try not to take over or anything. I haven’t really noticed it as a big problem. Is that okay to say?
Do you often find yourself running or climbing, even when it's not necessarily appropriate or expected?

Not really running or climbing, no… I wouldn’t want to make it sound like I’m doing that. It’s more like I feel restless, like there’s a motor going inside me all day. If I have to sit still at church, or here at the clinic, or even at home, I start feeling kind of trapped and like I need to get up or do something. Is that what you mean?
Do you often interrupt others when they're speaking?

Yeah… I try not to, but I think I do that. Like I’ll jump in with an answer before the pastor is finished, or my cousin, or even the lady at the pantry, and then I realize I answered the wrong thing or I kind of cut them off. Sometimes they get irritated, and I feel bad after. I’m not trying to be rude, it just comes out before I stop myself.
Do you often feel like you're constantly on the go, even when you're not supposed to be?

Yeah… I guess that’s probably the main thing. I try to sit and act normal, but inside it feels like I’ve got a motor running all day. Like at church, or even here at the clinic, or just at home, if I have to sit still too long I start feeling trapped, like I need to get up or do something. I don’t mean to make it sound dramatic, but that’s kind of why I came in. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking?
Do you often dominate conversations or have trouble letting others speak?

I don’t mean to dominate, no… at least I don’t think I’m trying to. But I do jump in too much. Like with the pastor, or my cousin, or the lady at the pantry, I’ll answer before they’re even done talking, and then I realize I got it wrong or I cut them off. Sometimes they look mad, and I feel bad. I’m trying to listen better, but it kind of comes out fast.
Do you often talk excessively, to the point where others have trouble getting a word in?

Um… I don’t know if I’d say excessively. I mean, I do talk when I’m nervous, probably more than I should sometimes, but I’m not sure if people can’t get a word in. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. Maybe you’d have to ask them, I guess. Is that what you mean?
Do you often blurt out answers before the other person has finished asking the question?

Yeah… I do that. I don’t mean it rude, but I’ll jump in with an answer before they’re even done asking. Like with the pastor, my cousin, or the pantry lady, I think I know what they’re saying and I answer, and then I realize I answered the wrong thing… or I made them mad. I feel bad after. Is that what you mean?
Do you think your restlessness and need to get up or do something is more because you get bored easily or because you just can't seem to sit still?

I think it’s more like I just can’t sit still… I mean, I do get bored, sure, but it feels more like there’s a motor running inside me all day. If I’m sitting at church, or here at the clinic, or even at home, I start feeling kind of trapped, like I have to get up or do something. I’m not trying to be disrespectful or anything… it’s just hard to stay put. Is that what you’re asking?
Do you think your difficulty paying attention is as bothersome to you as your restlessness and need to move around?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, the moving around feels more obvious, like people can see that, so I notice it more. But the paying attention part does bother me too.

Like when folks are talking about ride times, or the pantry list, or plans at church, I’ll be listening good at first, I really will… and then my mind just kind of slips off. Then I miss pieces I needed to hear, and I feel bad asking again. So, yeah, I guess it is pretty bothersome too, just maybe not as loud as the restless part. Is that answering it right?
Do you think your difficulty paying attention is more of a problem for you than your restlessness?

I’m not sure it’s more of a problem than the restlessness… but it is a problem, yeah.

Like I’ll be trying to listen when people are going over ride times, or the pantry list, or plans at church, and at first I’m with them. Then my mind just kind of slips off somewhere, and I miss parts I really needed to hear. I don’t mean to. I try to act like I got it, but then I realize I didn’t catch something important.

So… maybe not more than the moving around, but it does mess me up. Does that make sense?
Do you think your difficulty paying attention is significantly impacting your daily life?

Yeah… I think it is. I don’t like saying it like that, because I really do try to help and be useful.

But people at church, and at the pantry, and even my family… they don’t really trust me as much with rides, appointments, or keeping track of supplies anymore. I’ll mean to do it right, but I miss something or forget part of what was said, and then it causes trouble for somebody.

I feel bad about it. Like I keep letting everybody down, even when I’m trying. Does that make sense?
